key_insight: A high-fidelity remote controlled-Z gate can be performed between distant, frequency-tunable superconducting qubits using a multi-mode coaxial cable as the coupling channel.
engineering_relevance: This offers a simple route to modular superconducting processors by enabling nonlocal entangling operations without extra tunable couplers.
method: Use a multi-mode coaxial cable to mediate interaction between separated qubits
Apply an adiabatic gate protocol with frequency-tunable qubits
Numerically optimize the pulse for long cables and multiple standing-wave modes
evidence_signal: Simulations with ten cable modes for a 30-cm link report an optimized gate infidelity of 4.71×10^-7 and a 376.7 ns gate time without decoherence.
watch_item: Performance is shown in simulation, so real hardware must still manage decoherence, calibration, and sensitivity to cable fabrication tolerances.
paper_title: Remote Adiabatic Controlled-Z Gate between Distant Superconducting Qubits
